chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The truthfulness of the statement is confirmed upon sneezing.'
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of sneezing in Islamic tradition regarding truthfulness?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) conveys that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) identified sneezing as a sign of truthfulness (tasdiq) in speech, reflecting the pre-Islamic Arab belief that Allah causes sneezing when one speaks the truth. This physical response is interpreted by Shia scholars as a divine confirmation of the speaker's veracity, linking bodily signs to spiritual integrity. The narration underscores the continuity of prophetic wisdom in recognizing natural phenomena as indicators of divine favor and truth.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘is sneezing is a sign of the truthfulness (of a speaker)’.
en.sarwar: 24. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfali from al-Sakuni from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:
‘‘The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘Sneezing is a sign of truthfulness.’”
